newsitem.title: BULGARIA: New Bulgaria cabinet says fuel crisis top priority.
newsitem.headline: New Bulgaria cabinet says fuel crisis top priority.

text.p: Bulgaria's new interim cabinet held its first meeting on Thursday and said alleviating the country's paralysing fuel crisis would be its first priority.

The cabinet, led by Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski, inherits economic chaos from the outgoing Socialist administration. Bulgaria has been without effective government since Zhan Videnov resigned as premier and party leader on December 21.

"It is paramount to sort out the situation with the fuel," Sofianski told a news conference. "We have information that many vital branches of the economy are on the verge of stopping operations due to the fuel shortage."

One of the new cabinet's first acts was to sack the board of directors of the Neftohim refinery, and Sofianski said he would visit the refinery at the Black Sea port of Bourgas later on Thursday to see its problems for himself.

Regular government price revisions cannot keep up with the collapse of the lev and Neftohim has no money to import crude or settle its huge debts to suppliers. Most petrol stations are closed and public transport is reducing services.

The cabinet also set up a Financial Stabilisation Council headed by Sofianski and including Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriisky, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov, Chavdar Kanchev, director of Bulgarian foreign trade bank Bulbank, and former debt negotiator Ventsislav Antonov.
The council will implement financial stabilisation policy and negotiate with international lenders.

Missions are expected in the next few days from the European Union, and from the International Monetary Fund, which suspended credits last year because of the Socialists' failure to carry out promised reforms.
Sofianski said the council would hold its first meeting on Friday and whether to lift price controls on certain items would be one subject for discussion.
"We will have a clear position on all issues in two to three days," Sofianski said.

After 30 days of mass protests fuelled by economic hardship, the Socialist majority last week gave up efforts to form a new cabinet and agreed to elections 20 months before the end of their parliamentary term.
President Petar Stoyanov appointed the caretaker cabinet on Wednesday, setting elections for April 19 and dissolving parliament with effect from February 19.

The outgoing parliament, wrapping up outstanding business, voted to lower the barrier for parties to enter parliament to three percent from four percent of the vote, paving the way for smaller parties to enter the assembly.
